content.value: A read-time node standing in for a Dangling Reference target the Content Edges Table FK could never store — drawn dashed and muted, never expandable.

FK forbids storing an edge to a missing target, so the Content Edges Table never holds a dangling row. But a Reference Field in a Document's payload can still *point* at a deleted or unpublished target. To show that link honestly, Graph Traversal computes a
— a synthetic node representing the unresolvable target. There is no
column; the phantom exists only for the duration of the query.
The Graph Renderer draws a phantom in a distinct style —
— so it reads as "this points somewhere that isn't there." It participates in the Force Simulation layout but is
: you cannot traverse through it, because there is nothing real on the other side. Clicking it does not deepen the BFS.
A phantom is a *target* that should exist but doesn't; an Orphan Node is a real Document that simply has no edges at all. Different absences, different styling.

Blast Radius is the tool that warns you *before* you create one — removing a referenced target turns every referrer's edge into a future phantom. In real prod data, the Dangling Reference count behind phantoms was a small handful.
